academy.name: ANC CC Ops Academy
academy.tagline: Campaign Communications Command Centre Operations & Digital Governance
academy.hero_description: The training curriculum for the people who operate ANC CC Ops, the Campaign Communications Command Centre built by CEDEC Africa: national communicators, war room and rapid-response staff, desk operators, provincial and regional DCIPs, investigators and administrators.
academy.certification: CEDEC Africa Certified Campaign Operations Specialist (CCOS)

lessons.title: System Overview: Desks, Roles & the Sign-Off Gate
lessons.subtitle: One web console, its desks, the roles accounts carry, and which modules a deployment switches on
lessons.overview: ANC CC Ops is one web application for running a campaign's communications, built by CEDEC Africa. Its core desks are Daily Ops & Review (the Weekly Campaign Order, the day's decision, the review queue and the message bank), the 2-Hour Rapid Rebuttal, the WeVote Chatbot desk with the Social Media Army, the 07:00 Morning Intel and Administration. Facebook ads, Investigations, Wards, Manifestos, DCIP and the WhatsApp Cloud API bot are additional modules that each deployment switches on or off. Accounts are issued by an administrator, each carries one or more roles, and actions that need authority are signed off by a person in a role they hold.
keyPoints: Roles defined in the code: National Communications Director, Elections Committee Operations Lead, Head of Media Relations Desk, SG / TG Authorised Representative, Rapid-Response Lead, Fact-Check Officer, Spokesperson, Investigations Coordinator, Investigator, WhatsApp Desk Operator, Campaign Manager, War Room Coordinator, Provincial DCIP and Regional DCIP, plus the admin and super_admin roles
A Provincial or Regional DCIP account is scoped to an area (a province or region); other accounts act nationally
The sign-off gate records who signed, in which role, which action on which subject, and three certifications; each sign-off is used once, for one action

Each module has a feature flag. The core desks are on by default; Facebook ads is off by default, and Investigations, Wards, Manifestos, DCIP and the WhatsApp Cloud API bot are on by default but can be switched off. A switched-off desk has no tab and its API answers 404
The ☰ menu also opens the Media Asset Bank Vault and the User Guide & SOP Manual
operationalProcedures: 1. Sign in with the email address on your account; the header chip shows your name, roles and, for a DCIP, your area.
2. Move between desks with the tab buttons under the header or the Desks section of the ☰ menu. Only the desks switched on for this deployment are listed.
3. Before acting, check which of your roles the action needs: the gate's 'Signing as' list offers only roles your account holds, and the approval ladder limits who may sign each class of content.
4. If a desk you expect is missing, ask the administrator whether that module is switched on for this deployment.
takeaways: Never share your sign-in or sign off on someone else's behalf: every sign-off is recorded against the person who made it, in the role they chose.
Not every action goes through the gate: a Counter Active Playbook dispatch, a DCIP hub dispatch and a one-to-one WhatsApp reply, among others, are recorded in the audit trail without a sign-off.
Which desks you see depends on the deployment's feature flags, not only on your roles.

quiz.question: Which of the following is NOT a role defined in ANC CC Ops?
quiz.explanation: War Room Coordinator, Rapid-Response Lead and Fact-Check Officer are in the role list in src/auth/accounts.ts. There is no Chief Digital Strategist role.

quiz.question: When you sign off an action, which roles does the 'Signing as' list offer you?
options: Every role defined in the system
Only the roles your own account holds
Only the role that owns the desk you are on
Only the National Communications Director role
quiz.explanation: The gate lists only the roles your account holds (it does not offer the admin role), and the server refuses a sign-off in a role you do not hold.

lessons.title: Access, Sign-In & Account Security
lessons.subtitle: The UAT access gate, email sign-in, passkeys, sessions and password rules
lessons.overview: On UAT an access gate sits in front of the sign-in page, and its key is handed over by the operator. Behind it, you sign in with the email address on your account and your password, or with a passkey you have enrolled. There is no self-registration and no password reset on the sign-in page: accounts are issued by the administrator.
keyPoints: Sign-in takes an email address; usernames are refused with a message asking for the email address
Passkeys (WebAuthn: Touch ID, Windows Hello or a security key) can be enrolled from the ☰ menu under 'Passkeys / Biometrics'
Ten failed attempts from one address lock that address out for fifteen minutes
A session is an HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookie (Secure in production mode) lasting twelve hours and refreshed while you use it
Passwords are at least 12 characters and stored only as scrypt hashes
operationalProcedures: 1. Open the command centre address. On UAT, enter the access gate key you were given.
2. On the 'Sign in' page, type your email address and password and click 'Sign in', or click 'Sign in with a Passkey' if you have enrolled one.
3. If you are asked to change your password, open the ☰ menu and choose 'Change password'. Under the UAT access lock the issued password is final and cannot be changed.
4. Check the header chip: your name, your roles and, for a DCIP, your area.
5. When you finish, open the ☰ menu and choose 'Sign out'.
takeaways: Lost your password? Ask the administrator; there is no reset on the sign-in page.
Outside the UAT access lock, an administrator can reset a password or deactivate an account, and either ends that account's sessions.
Sign-ins, refused sign-ins and password changes are written to the access log with the address they came from.

quiz.question: What do you type in the sign-in form's identifier field?
options: The email address on your account
quiz.explanation: Sign-in is email-only; a username is refused with a message asking for the email address.

quiz.question: What happens after ten failed sign-in attempts from one address?
options: That address is locked out for fifteen minutes
The administrator must reset the password
quiz.explanation: The limiter in src/auth/limiter.ts locks an address for fifteen minutes after ten failures.

quiz.question: How long does a session last?
options: Twelve hours, refreshed while you use it
quiz.explanation: Sessions are twelve hours long and refreshed on use (src/auth/session.ts); signing out ends them sooner.

lessons.title: The Sign-Off Gate: Three Certifications, One Use
lessons.subtitle: What the gate records, the approval ladder, and the actions that do not pass through it
lessons.overview: Actions that need authority, such as logging or closing a rebuttal situation, signing or dispatching a stage, approving a draft or a message-bank line, issuing the Weekly Campaign Order, signing a localisation, approving an issue brief, sending a broadcast or posting instruction, opening or closing an investigation and creating a paid campaign, pass through the 'Executive Confirmation & Human Sign-Off' window. The server records the sign-off and the action consumes it exactly once. Not every action passes through the gate: Counter Active Playbook dispatches and DCIP desk dispatches do not, and neither do one-to-one WhatsApp replies.
keyPoints: The record holds who signed, the role they signed as, the action, the subject and the three certifications
Certification 1, Truth Matrix & Factual Grounding: the content is verified against the Message Bank and public records
Certification 2, IEC Electoral Code Adherence: compliance with the Electoral Act, with no defamatory or false statements
Certification 3, POPIA Data Privacy: recipient lists operate under verified opt-in consent
A sign-off cannot be reused, used by another person, or presented for a different subject or action

The approval ladder sets who may sign each content class: routine (any sign-off role), localised (Provincial or Regional DCIP within their area, or national), rapid response, major campaign creative, and PA/PEB and paid national (SG / TG Authorised Representative)
operationalProcedures: 1. Click the action button on the desk (for example '✅ Approve', '✍️ Sign off' or '⚡ Log it and start the clock').
2. Read the 'ACTION TO BE SIGNED OFF' summary.
3. Tick all three certifications; none is pre-ticked.
4. In 'Signing as', choose the role you are acting in.
5. Click '✅ Authorise & Execute Action', or 'Cancel / Review Draft' to go back without signing.
takeaways: A gated action without a valid, unused sign-off is refused by the server.
If you cannot honestly tick a certification, do not sign: return to the draft.
Counter Active Playbook and DCIP dispatches are not signed off. The review items and posting instructions a playbook creates arrive as drafts that still need approval through the gate.

quiz.question: What happens to a sign-off once the action it authorised has been carried out?
options: It is consumed and cannot be used again
It transfers to the next person in the queue
It is deleted from the record
quiz.explanation: consumeSignoff in src/signoff.ts marks the sign-off consumed; presenting it again is refused as already used.

quiz.question: Which of these is one of the three certifications in the gate?
quiz.explanation: The three are Truth Matrix & Factual Grounding, IEC Electoral Code Adherence and POPIA Data Privacy.

quiz.question: Which of these actions does NOT pass through the sign-off gate?
options: Dispatching a pack to a provincial hub on the DCIP desk
quiz.explanation: The DCIP desk's dispatch routes record the dispatch without a sign-off; the other three require one.

lessons.title: Daily Ops & Review Desk: Campaign Command, Schedule & Message Bank
lessons.subtitle: Weekly Campaign Order, the 08:00 decision, the night assessment, the review queue and the message bank
lessons.overview: The Daily Ops & Review Desk is where the campaign is commanded. Its Campaign command panel holds the Weekly Campaign Order, the day's 08:00 decision and night assessment, provincial and regional localisation, issue briefs, the content factory and the Counter Active Playbook. Beside it sit the day's schedule, the review queue where drafts are approved or rejected, the message bank of approved lines and the press list.
keyPoints: Campaign command tabs: Today, Weekly order, Localisation, Issue briefs, Content factory and ⚡ Counter Active Playbook

The Weekly Campaign Order has thirteen elements; it is drafted by the National Communications Director, War Room Coordinator, Campaign Manager or Elections Committee Operations Lead, and issued through the gate by the National Communications Director or the SG / TG Authorised Representative
Only the War Room Coordinator or the National Communications Director records the 08:00 decision and the night assessment
Review queue items are pending, approved or rejected; message-bank lines are draft, approved or retired, and editing an approved line returns it to draft
The message bank is searchable by text, tags and keywords, and filterable by issue and audience
operationalProcedures: 1. Check the Weekly order tab for this week's issued order; without one, the day runs within the general playbook.
2. Review the day's Schedule and add items with '+ Add to schedule'.

3. At 08:00 the War Room Coordinator or National Communications Director records the decision: the day's Counter Active proposition, what must be rebutted, what should be ignored and why, what must be localised and who carries the message.
4. Under 'Morning · Deploy', draft the morning's products; each goes to the review queue, and approved products make up the daily pack.
5. Search the message bank before writing new lines; submit new text to the review queue and decide it through the gate.
6. In the evening, record the night assessment: what moved, what underperformed, what narrative is rising, what must change tomorrow.
takeaways: Speak from approved message-bank lines where they exist; a new line is approved through the gate before it is used.
An issued order is not edited: draft and issue a replacement.
Only roles on an item's approval class can approve it.

quiz.question: What is the message bank for?
options: Holding the approved lines the desks speak from
quiz.explanation: The message bank holds lines with draft, approved or retired status; approved lines are what drafting and the WhatsApp desk use.

quiz.question: Who records the 08:00 decision on the Daily Ops desk?
options: The War Room Coordinator or the National Communications Director
quiz.explanation: DAY_DECIDERS in content/ops-desk.js and src/campaign/routes.ts name only these two roles.

quiz.question: What happens when you edit the text of an approved message-bank line?
options: The line returns to draft and must be approved again
Nothing; approved lines cannot be edited
quiz.explanation: Changing the title or text of an approved line sets it back to draft (src/bank/routes.ts).

lessons.title: 2-Hour Rapid Rebuttal: The Five-Stage Clock
lessons.subtitle: Logging a situation, the five stage marks, dispatch, and the Counter Active Playbook
lessons.overview: When a hostile claim breaks, a situation is logged on the 2-Hour Rapid Rebuttal desk through the sign-off gate, and a 120-minute clock starts. Five stage deliverables fall due at fixed marks after logging, each owned by a role, each drafted, edited and signed off before it can be dispatched on its own channels. Separately, the Counter Active Playbook on the Daily Ops desk turns a breaking story into attack lines, cross-desk directives and a spokesperson pack.
keyPoints: Stage 1, Fact check, due at +15 minutes: Fact-Check Officer; nothing leaves the desk
Stage 2, Holding statement, due at +30 minutes: National Communications Director; press wire (email) and X
Stage 3, Spokesperson media pack, due at +60 minutes: Spokesperson; press wire
Stage 4, Digital & grassroots cascade, due at +90 minutes: Rapid-Response Lead; X, plus Facebook and WhatsApp where those modules are switched on
Stage 5, Visual rebuttal card, due at +118 minutes: Rapid-Response Lead; same channels as stage 4
Five minutes before a stage's mark, and again when it is missed, the stage owner's role, the Rapid-Response Lead and the person who logged the situation are notified
operationalProcedures: 1. Click '+ Log a situation', fill in the title, the claim as made, where it was seen, the link, what is true, and the severity, then '⚡ Log it and start the clock' and sign off through the gate.
2. Add facts and attach material under 'Update the facts / attach material'.
3. Open each stage, draft it with '🤖 Draft from the facts' where drafting is configured or write it yourself, save, and sign it off through the gate.
4. Dispatch a signed stage on one of its channels and sign the dispatch; read the result: sent, refused or failed.
5. Use the briefing pack, the contrast card and the Markdown pack for the spokesperson, then close the situation through the gate.

6. For a Counter Active Playbook, open the '⚡ Counter Active Playbook' tab on the Daily Ops desk, generate it from a URL, topic or notes, and dispatch its directives. These dispatches do not pass through the sign-off gate; the review items and posting instructions they create still need approval.
takeaways: The clock is a set of marks with alerts, not an automatic action: a missed mark is reported, and the stage still needs a person to finish it.
Release the holding statement by its +30 mark; the Morning Intel shows the seven-day average time from logging to holding-statement sign-off.
A playbook's 'rebuttal' directive creates a situation directly, without the logging sign-off.

quiz.question: When is the holding statement due?
options: 15 minutes after the situation is logged
30 minutes after the situation is logged
2 hours after the situation is logged
24 hours after the situation is logged
quiz.explanation: In src/rebuttal/stages.ts the holding statement (stage 2) is due 30 minutes after logging.

quiz.question: Which role owns the stage 1 fact check?
quiz.explanation: Stage 1 is owned by the Fact-Check Officer, and its deliverable has no dispatch channels.

quiz.question: Which statement about Counter Active Playbook dispatches is correct?
options: They are signed off through the gate like every other action
They do not pass through the sign-off gate; the drafts they create still need approval
They publish directly to X and Facebook
They can only be sent by the administrator
quiz.explanation: dispatchPlaybook in src/ops/playbook-engine.ts consumes no sign-off; review items and posting instructions it creates arrive as drafts.

lessons.title: WeVote Chatbot Desk & the Social Media Army
lessons.subtitle: The public web chatbot, the test bot, citizen messages, broadcasts and volunteer posting instructions
lessons.overview: The WeVote chatbot is a public, browser-based chat that needs no account: a citizen picks a local area and asks about candidates, the local manifesto or volunteering. It runs in the browser rather than through the WhatsApp Cloud API. The WeVote Chatbot desk opens it, and also carries the WhatsApp Cloud API tools (test bot, waiting queue, conversations and broadcasts, which are part of the whatsapp_bot module and must be enabled for the deployment) and the Social Media Army's distribution lists and posting instructions.
keyPoints: The public chatbot answers manifesto questions from retrieved manifesto excerpts and finds ward candidates from the candidate records
The Test Bot (RAG Simulator) shows the grounding citations behind an answer and reaches no citizen
Contacts carry a consent state: opted in, opted out or unknown. Replying STOP (or one of the other stop words) opts a contact out
Broadcasts are at most 140 words, go only to opted-in contacts, and are sent through the gate
Social Media Army: lists of opted-in contacts by area and role, posting instructions (with PI references) sent through the gate, and posted links reported back and recorded
operationalProcedures: 1. Click '🚀 Open Live Chatbot' to open the public chatbot, or '📢 View Campaign Advert' for the advert page.
2. Test answers in '🤖 Test Bot (RAG Simulator)' and read the '📚 Grounding Citations'.
3. Work '⏳ Waiting for a person' and '💬 Conversation' for messages the bank could not answer; an opted-out contact cannot be messaged.
4. Draft a broadcast in '📣 Broadcasts' and send it to opted-in contacts through the gate.
5. In '👥 Lists' build a list, then in '📲 Posting instructions' write one and send it to the list through the gate; record links reported back.
takeaways: One-to-one replies to a contact are recorded in the thread and audit trail but do not pass through the sign-off gate; broadcasts and posting instructions do.
Outside 24 hours since a contact last wrote, only an approved WhatsApp template can carry a message.
If the Test Bot, Waiting, Conversation or Broadcasts tabs show an error, the WhatsApp Cloud API module is switched off for this deployment.

quiz.question: Who receives a WhatsApp broadcast sent from the desk?
options: Every contact who has ever written in
Only contacts whose consent state is opted in
quiz.explanation: The broadcast route counts and targets only contacts with consent_state 'opted_in'.

quiz.question: What does the Test Bot (RAG Simulator) do?
options: Sends a message to a random citizen
Shows how the bot would answer for a chosen municipality, with its citations, without messaging anyone
quiz.explanation: Test answers appear with their grounding citations and reach no citizen.

quiz.question: What happens when a contact replies STOP?
options: The contact is opted out and is not messaged
The contact is added to a volunteer list
quiz.explanation: STOP and the other stop words in src/whatsapp/matcher.ts set the contact to opted out; the reply route refuses opted-out contacts.

lessons.title: 07:00 Morning Intel: Desk Figures & Fourteen-Day Activity
lessons.subtitle: Figures computed from the desks' own records, with 'no data' where nothing was recorded
lessons.overview: The 07:00 Morning Intel desk shows the state of the campaign's desks from what they recorded: rebuttal situations and stage timing, dispatches by channel, WhatsApp traffic and consent, investigation evidence and the review queue. It is computed when the desk is opened and refreshes every 30 seconds while it is open; it is read before the morning briefing rather than delivered.
keyPoints: Figures: Situations open (and how many are past the two-hour SLA), Holding statement average, Stages on time, Dispatched in 24 h (with refused and failed), WhatsApp in 24 h, Opted-in contacts, Evidence tone over 7 days, and the Review queue
A 'Fourteen days' chart of situations logged, dispatches sent, WhatsApp messages in and evidence items
'Dispatch by channel, 7 days', 'What channels reported' and 'Investigations' panels
'↻ Fetch channel metrics' (for administrators, not shown on UAT) asks each connected channel what it reports for what was sent
operationalProcedures: 1. Open '07:00 Morning Intel' before the morning briefing.
2. Check Situations open and how many are past the SLA, and the holding-statement average against the 30-minute mark.
3. Check dispatches by channel for refusals and failures, and the review queue for items waiting.
4. Use the fourteen-day chart to see the tempo of situations, dispatches, WhatsApp traffic and evidence.
takeaways: A panel with nothing recorded behind it reads 'no data'; the desk does not estimate.
On UAT, channels without settings simulate their sends and reach figures, so UAT numbers are not evidence of real reach.
Evidence tone is the mean tone of investigation evidence, from −1 hostile to +1 favourable.

quiz.question: What does a Morning Intel panel show when nothing behind it was recorded?
options: An estimate based on last week
quiz.explanation: The telemetry desk shows 'no data' for missing figures and never estimates.

quiz.question: Where do the Morning Intel figures come from?
options: A report emailed by a third party at 07:00
The desks' own records (situations, dispatches, WhatsApp messages, evidence, review items)
Manual entry by the administrator each morning
quiz.explanation: src/telemetry/routes.ts computes every figure from the application's own tables when the desk asks.

quiz.question: How often does the desk refresh while it is open?
options: Only when you reload the page
quiz.explanation: content/telemetry-desk.js polls every 30 seconds while the desk is open.

lessons.title: Facebook Campaign Manager: Drafting Paid Campaigns
lessons.subtitle: An optional module: draft, ask Meta for the estimate, create paused after sign-off
lessons.overview: The Facebook Campaign Manager is an additional module that is switched off by default (ANCOPS_FEATURE_FBADS). It must be enabled for the deployment before its tab appears; while it is off, its tab is absent and its API answers 404. When enabled, it drafts a paid campaign, stores Meta's reach estimate, and after sign-off creates the campaign paused in Ads Manager under the issues, elections and politics special ad category. A person switches it on in Ads Manager.
keyPoints: Off by default; the desk must be enabled for the deployment
Draft fields: name, objective, days, provinces (none means all of South Africa), age range, gender, daily budget in rand, ad text, headline and link
'📈 Ask Meta for the estimate' needs the Marketing API connected; without it the desk shows no number in its place
'Create in Ads Manager (paused)' passes through the sign-off gate
While the module is off, the Facebook Page channel is also not offered on rebuttal stages
operationalProcedures: 1. Confirm with the administrator that the module is enabled and the ad account connected for this deployment.
2. Under 'New campaign', fill in the fields and click 'Save draft'.
3. Click '📈 Ask Meta for the estimate' and read Meta's estimate as stored.
4. Click 'Create in Ads Manager (paused)' and sign off through the gate.
5. Download the '🖨️ Pack' or '⬇ JSON' record; a person switches the campaign on in Ads Manager.
takeaways: The desk never switches a campaign on; it is always created paused.
Ward links from the Wards desk only switch to this desk; targeting is set by province, age and gender here.

quiz.question: How is the Facebook Campaign Manager controlled?
options: By the ANCOPS_FEATURE_FBADS flag, off by default; while off its API answers 404 and its tab is absent
By a Facebook login on the server
It is removed from the code
quiz.explanation: src/features.ts sets fbads' default to off; requireFeature answers 404 while it is disabled.

quiz.question: In what state does the desk create a campaign in Ads Manager?
options: Paused, to be switched on by a person
quiz.explanation: The campaign is created PAUSED after sign-off (src/fbads/routes.ts).

quiz.question: What must happen before 'Create in Ads Manager (paused)' runs?
quiz.explanation: Creation consumes a 'fb_campaign' / 'create' sign-off.

lessons.title: Investigations Desk: Cases, Open-Source Search & Photo Tracing
lessons.subtitle: An optional module: purpose and lawful basis first, then searches, evidence and reports
lessons.overview: The Investigations Desk is an additional module (ANCOPS_FEATURE_OSINT). It is on by default but must be enabled for the deployment; when it is switched off, its tab is absent and its API answers 404. A case is opened through the sign-off gate with a stated purpose and a POPIA section 11 lawful basis. The desk then checks the configured open sources, keeps a versioned report, and lets you attach search results and traced photos as evidence.
keyPoints: Opening a case requires a purpose and a lawful basis; the server refuses a case without both
Subject types: narrative or story, leak, event, organisation, or a person in a public role
Media Search across the configured sources; results are attached to a case through the gate
Reverse Photo Forensics: a photo is hashed (SHA-256) and searched against reverse-image providers where configured, within an open case
Each case keeps a report, evidence, uploads, checks and an audit trail; a source whose provider is not configured is listed as not searched
operationalProcedures: 1. Click '➕ Open Investigation', describe the subject and question, choose sources and dates, state the purpose and choose the lawful basis, then open it and sign off through the gate.
2. In '🗂️ Case Files', read the report, evidence and checks; check again, keep monitoring or stop monitoring.
3. In '🔎 Media Search', search the sources and attach selected results to the case through the gate.
4. In '🖼️ Reverse Photo Forensics', choose the open case and drop a photo; attach the matches.
5. Close the case through the gate and download the report.
takeaways: The desk's own notice says it uses open sources only, accesses no account, contacts no one and never seeks special personal information; work within that.
Findings feed the Rapid Rebuttal desk: log the situation there with the facts the case established.

quiz.question: What must be recorded before an investigation can be opened?
options: A purpose and a POPIA section 11 lawful basis, then a sign-off
Approval from the WhatsApp Desk Operator
quiz.explanation: src/osint/routes.ts refuses a case without purpose and lawful basis, and opening consumes a sign-off.

quiz.question: If the Investigations module is switched off for a deployment, what happens?
options: The tab is absent and its API answers 404
It runs in the background anyway
quiz.explanation: requireFeature('osint') answers 404 and the tab is removed while the flag is off.

quiz.question: What does the desk do with a photo dropped into Reverse Photo Forensics?
options: Hashes it and searches it against the configured reverse-image providers within an open case
Edits it into a campaign graphic
Sends it to the press list
quiz.explanation: The image is hashed (SHA-256) and searched; matches can be attached to the case.

lessons.title: DCIP Digital Communications Desk
lessons.subtitle: An optional module: messaging packs, provincial hubs, government deliveries and the standalone dashboard
lessons.overview: The DCIP Digital Communications desk is an additional module (ANCOPS_FEATURE_DCIP). It is on by default but must be enabled for the deployment; when off, its tab, its standalone dashboard and its API answer not found. The desk carries the active key-messaging pack and its suggested posts, the nine provincial hubs, a queue of government delivery submissions, a roster of communicators and agency guidance. A standalone DCIP dashboard drafts new packs and takes government submissions.
keyPoints: Sections: 📦 Active Key-Messaging Pack, 🇿🇦 9 Provincial Hubs, 🏛️ Govt Deliveries Queue, 👥 Top Communicators Roster, 🤝 Agency & Listening
'🚀 Dispatch Pack to <province>' records the pack as dispatched to that hub
'✓ Verify' marks a government delivery submission as verified
The standalone dashboard drafts a messaging pack and accepts government delivery submissions
DCIP desk actions, including dispatches, do not pass through the sign-off gate
operationalProcedures: 1. Confirm the DCIP module is enabled for this deployment.
2. Read the active pack and copy suggested posts with '📋 Copy'.
3. Dispatch the pack to each provincial hub from '🇿🇦 9 Provincial Hubs'.
4. Check government delivery submissions and click '✓ Verify' once checked.
5. Open the standalone dashboard to draft a new weekly pack or submit a government delivery.
takeaways: Because DCIP dispatches are not signed off, check a pack before dispatching it.
The Provincial DCIP and Regional DCIP roles also sign localised content within their own area on the Daily Ops desk.

quiz.question: Which of these is a section of the DCIP desk?
quiz.explanation: content/dcip-desk.js has the pack, the 9 Provincial Hubs, the government deliveries queue, the communicators roster and agency & listening.

quiz.question: Does dispatching a pack to a provincial hub pass through the sign-off gate?
options: No; the dispatch is recorded without a sign-off
quiz.explanation: src/dcip/routes.ts records the hub dispatch without consuming a sign-off.

quiz.question: What happens on a deployment where the DCIP module is switched off?
options: The tab, the standalone dashboard and the API answer not found
quiz.explanation: server.ts returns 404 for /dcip and /api/dcip while the flag is off, and the tab is removed.

lessons.title: Wards, the Map & Candidate Records
lessons.subtitle: An optional module: 2,838 wards, 8,836 candidate records, ward dossiers
lessons.overview: The Wards & Geolocation desk is an additional module (ANCOPS_FEATURE_WARDS). It is on by default but must be enabled for the deployment. Its seed data holds 2,838 wards with their 2021 and 2024 results and 8,836 ANC candidate records (4,416 ward and 4,420 PR), all marked certified and locked. Wards are classed by ANC profile and shown on a map as points coloured by that class.
keyPoints: Ward tiers as the filter chips show them: '🟢 Safe' (Safe ANC, 643), '🟡 Strong' (Strong ANC, 1,435) and '🔴 Weak Battlegrounds' (Weak ANC, 760)
Views: '🗺️ Map', '📋 Wards' and '👥 Candidates (8,836)'; filter by tier, province, or search by IEC code, candidate name, ward or town
'Inspect' opens the WARD DOSSIER: vote shares, registered voters, candidates and the covering manifesto
The dossier buttons '🎯 Focus in Weekly Campaign Order', '📢 Mobilize WhatsApp Army List' and '📣 Micro-Target in Facebook Ads' only switch to that desk and show a note of the ward; they fill in nothing
Only Admin or Super Admin can edit a candidate record, and each change is written to the audit log
operationalProcedures: 1. Open '🗺️ Wards & Map (2,838)' and filter by tier chip, province or search.
2. Click 'Inspect' on a ward to read its dossier and candidates.
3. To act on a ward elsewhere, use a dossier button, then fill in the form on the desk it opens yourself.
4. Ask an administrator for any candidate record correction.
takeaways: The public chatbot's ward candidate lookup reads the same candidate records.
Tier labels classify the ANC's position in a ward; they are not a forecast.

quiz.question: How many wards does the Wards desk's data hold?
quiz.explanation: seed/wards.json holds 2,838 wards; 8,836 is the number of candidate records.

quiz.question: What does '📣 Micro-Target in Facebook Ads' in a ward dossier do?
options: Creates and launches an ad for that ward
Switches to the Facebook desk and shows a note of the ward; you fill in the form yourself
Deletes the ward from the map
quiz.explanation: ANCOPS_TARGET_WARD in content/wards-desk.js only switches desk and shows a toast.

quiz.question: Which label does the UI use for wards in the Weak ANC class?
quiz.explanation: The filter chip for Weak ANC wards reads '🔴 Weak Battlegrounds'.

lessons.title: Localised Manifestos & Grounded Answers
lessons.subtitle: An optional module: 52 municipal manifestos, 850 excerpts, retrieval with citations
lessons.overview: The Localised Manifestos desk is an additional module (ANCOPS_FEATURE_MANIFESTOS). It is on by default but must be enabled for the deployment. Its data holds 52 localised municipal manifestos across seven provinces, split into 850 excerpts. When the chatbot or the test bot answers a manifesto question, it retrieves matching excerpts by full-text search and either asks the configured drafting model to answer only from them, or, without a model, summarises the top excerpts directly. The citations are shown.
keyPoints: 52 manifestos across seven provinces and 850 excerpts in the seed data
Retrieval is PostgreSQL full-text search over the excerpts, narrowed to the citizen's municipality or province where known
The drafting model is instructed to answer only from the retrieved excerpts; without a model, the answer is built from the excerpts themselves
Filter the catalogue by province, locality type or search; 'Inspect Dossier' and '⬇️ Doc' open or download a manifesto
'🤖 Test in WhatsApp Bot Simulator' uses the test bot, which is part of the WhatsApp Cloud API module
operationalProcedures: 1. Open '📘 Manifestos (52 Municipal)' and filter by province, locality type or search.
2. Click 'Inspect Dossier' to read a municipality's commitments, or '⬇️ Doc' to download it.
3. Test questions against it in the test bot and read the grounding citations.
4. Quote the manifesto's own words in statements, and check a model's answer against its citations.
takeaways: Instructions reduce but do not remove a model's errors: check answers against the cited excerpts.
Localised commitments are the source for local lines; national lines come from the message bank.

quiz.question: What grounds the chatbot's manifesto answers?
options: Manifesto excerpts retrieved by full-text search, which the model is told to answer from and which are shown as citations
quiz.explanation: src/campaign/manifesto-rag.ts retrieves excerpts and instructs the model to answer only from them; the citations are returned.

quiz.question: How many localised manifestos does the desk hold?
quiz.explanation: seed/manifestos.json holds 52 manifestos and 850 excerpts.

quiz.question: What happens to a manifesto question when no drafting model is configured?
options: The answer is built directly from the top retrieved excerpts
The question is emailed to the administrator
quiz.explanation: Without a model, answerManifestoQuery falls back to a summary made from the retrieved excerpts.

lessons.title: Channels, Drafting & What Happens When a Setting Is Missing
lessons.subtitle: Channel adapters, status pills, refused and failed dispatches, and UAT simulation
lessons.overview: Each outbound channel is a separate adapter: the press wire (email through the shared mail relay), X (Twitter), the Facebook Page and WhatsApp Business. Drafting uses a configured model, and the Investigations desk uses configured search providers. Every dispatch attempt is recorded: sent, refused (the channel has no settings) or failed (the provider's error). On UAT, or where simulation is switched on, a channel without settings simulates its send instead, and nothing is published.
keyPoints: Status pills on the Rapid Rebuttal desk show each channel and drafting as 'ready' or 'not configured'
A channel button without settings reads '(unavailable)' and is disabled
A dispatch is recorded as sent (with the provider's id), refused (with the missing setting named) or failed (with the provider's error)
The Facebook Page channel is offered on a rebuttal stage only when the Facebook ads module is switched on, and WhatsApp only when the WhatsApp Cloud API module is
Without a drafting model, stages and drafts are written by hand and '🤖 Draft from the facts' is disabled
operationalProcedures: 1. Read the status pills before you start a dispatch.
2. If a channel shows 'not configured', use another channel the stage allows, or ask the administrator to connect it.
3. After each dispatch, read the dispatch line: sent, refused or failed, and why.
4. Never put tokens or keys into a draft, a note or a chat; the administrator adds channel settings to the deployment's environment.
takeaways: Connecting a channel is a configuration change by the administrator, not a code change.
A refused or failed dispatch published nothing on that channel; it does not stop the rest of the desk.
On UAT, a 'sent' from a channel without settings is a simulation.

quiz.question: What happens when a dispatch is attempted on a channel that has no settings, outside UAT?
options: The dispatch is recorded as refused, naming the missing setting
The system reports a fake success
The message is sent from a personal account
quiz.explanation: dispatch() in src/channels/registry.ts records a refusal row when the adapter is unconfigured.

quiz.question: On UAT, what does a channel without settings do when a stage is dispatched?
options: It simulates the send; nothing is published
quiz.explanation: isUatOrSimulated() in src/channels/types.ts makes unconfigured adapters return a simulated result on UAT.

quiz.question: When is the WhatsApp channel offered on a rebuttal stage?
options: Only when the WhatsApp Cloud API module is switched on
quiz.explanation: activeChannels() in src/rebuttal/stages.ts drops WhatsApp while the whatsapp_bot flag is off.

lessons.title: POPIA, Consent & the Audit Record
lessons.subtitle: Consent states, opt-out, the gate's certifications, lawful basis and what is recorded
lessons.overview: The command centre records consent for every WhatsApp contact, sends broadcasts and posting instructions only to opted-in contacts, and refuses to message a contact who has opted out. The gate's POPIA certification asks the signer to confirm that recipient lists operate under opt-in consent, and investigations record a POPIA section 11 lawful basis before they start. Actions are written to audit trails: sign-ins and administrative changes to the access log with the address they came from, and desk actions to each subject's audit trail.
keyPoints: Consent states are opted in, opted out and unknown; a consent change asks how consent was established and records the answer
STOP and the other stop words opt a contact out before any reply is sent
Broadcasts go only to opted-in contacts; replies to opted-out contacts are refused
Investigations require a purpose and a POPIA section 11 lawful basis, and a person is a subject only in their public role
The access log records sign-ins, refusals and administrative changes with the source address; desk audit trails record who did what and when
operationalProcedures: 1. Message only contacts who have written to the official number, and broadcast only to those opted in.
2. When a contact asks to stop, make sure they are set to opted out; a STOP reply does this automatically.
3. When you change a contact's consent by hand, record how consent was established.
4. Tick the gate's IEC and POPIA certifications only when they are true for what you are signing.
takeaways: Consent and lawful basis are recorded so that each decision can be shown later.
Not every action is signed off, but desk actions are recorded in the audit trail.

quiz.question: Which contacts receive a WhatsApp broadcast?
options: Opted-out contacts, to confirm their choice
quiz.explanation: The broadcast route targets only consent_state 'opted_in'.

quiz.question: What does the access log record for a sign-in?
options: The outcome, the account and the address it came from
quiz.explanation: estateAudit in src/auth/accounts.ts writes event, outcome, subject, actor and source address.

quiz.question: What must an investigation record before it starts?
options: A purpose and a POPIA section 11 lawful basis
quiz.explanation: The Investigations desk refuses a case without purpose and lawful basis.

lessons.title: Administration: Accounts, Campaign Settings & Regions
lessons.subtitle: Issuing accounts with roles and areas, the campaign calendar, regions and the access log
lessons.overview: The Administration desk is open to accounts holding the admin role, from the ☰ menu under Account. Its tabs are Accounts, Campaign settings, Regions, Access log and AI & Background Engine. Accounts are issued here and nowhere else; under the UAT access lock an administrator can still issue accounts but cannot reset passwords or deactivate accounts.
keyPoints: Issue an account with a username (display handle), full name, email (used to sign in), one or more roles, and an area: National, or a province or region for a Provincial or Regional DCIP
An initial password is at least 12 characters, and is shown once; 'Must change it on first sign-in' is offered when the access lock is off
Campaign settings: campaign name, organisation, campaign line, polls date (the header countdown), election day and special vote days
Campaign phases are date ranges (five by default); the phase in effect follows today's date, and the administrator edits the list
Regions can be added, renamed, retired once empty, have municipalities moved between them, or be imported from CSV
operationalProcedures: 1. Open the ☰ menu and choose 'Administration'.
2. In 'Accounts', issue an account with the right roles and area, and hand the email and password to the person privately.
3. Use 'Roles / area' to change an account; outside the access lock, use 'Reset password', 'Deactivate' or 'Reactivate' as needed.
4. In 'Campaign settings', keep the dates, the campaign line and the phases correct.
5. In 'Access log', review sign-ins, refusals and administrative changes regularly.
takeaways: Deactivating an account or resetting its password ends that account's sessions immediately.
Phases change with the calendar; editing the phases changes which one is shown on the desks.
An administrator cannot remove their own admin role or deactivate themselves.

quiz.question: What happens when an administrator deactivates an account (outside the UAT access lock)?
options: The account's sessions end immediately and it can no longer sign in
The account is given to someone else
The person receives a warning letter
quiz.explanation: src/admin/routes.ts revokes the account's sessions on deactivation, and inactive accounts are refused at session lookup.

quiz.question: What decides which campaign phase is in effect?
options: A button the administrator presses to advance the phase
Today's date against the phases' date ranges
quiz.explanation: primaryPhase() in src/campaign/calendar.ts picks the phase whose dates include today.

quiz.question: Under the UAT access lock, which administrative action is refused?
quiz.explanation: Under the lock, password resets and deactivations are refused; issuing accounts is still allowed.
